scope: Eighteen additional glossary entries verified from public primary or issuing-authority sources. Definitions only; no response criteria, score thresholds, derivations, risk assignment, clinical-record searches, or application edits.
integration_note: Add to the existing dictionary without replacing its existing entries. DEXA and DXA are aliases of one glossary entry. A verified expansion does not verify an unknown source field's meaning.

glossary.definition: A prognostic staging system for multiple myeloma based on serum beta-2 microglobulin and albumin.
glossary.sourceLabel: Greipp et al., International staging system for multiple myeloma (J Clin Oncol, 2005; PubMed)
glossary.caveat: Use this expansion only in the myeloma staging context. ISS can denote other concepts elsewhere. Preserve the recorded system and stage; do not infer a stage from this definition.

glossary.definition: A revised prognostic staging system for newly diagnosed multiple myeloma that incorporates ISS, selected cytogenetic abnormalities, and lactate dehydrogenase.
glossary.sourceLabel: Palumbo et al., Revised International Staging System for Multiple Myeloma (J Clin Oncol, 2015; PubMed)
glossary.caveat: R-ISS is a specific revision and is distinct from ISS and R2-ISS. No stage, cytogenetic category, or prognosis is assigned here.

glossary.definition: A treatment response in which detectable signs of cancer have disappeared; also called complete remission.
glossary.sourceLabel: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: complete response

supportingSources.label: International Myeloma Foundation, ONS 2023 educational slides: CR abbreviation

glossary.caveat: CR may be expanded as complete response or complete remission in a source. It does not mean cure. The disease, assessment method, and source-specific response framework remain necessary.

glossary.definition: A distinct, more stringent complete-response category used in International Myeloma Working Group assessment of myeloma treatment response.
glossary.sourceLabel: International Myeloma Working Group / International Myeloma Foundation: uniform response criteria

supportingSources.label: International Myeloma Foundation, ONS 2023 educational slides: sCR abbreviation

glossary.caveat: Retain the lower-case s in the display token. This label alone does not establish cure, MRD negativity, or which response-criteria version was used.

glossary.definition: A treatment-related reduction in tumour size or the extent of cancer; also called partial remission.
glossary.sourceLabel: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: partial response

supportingSources.label: International Myeloma Foundation, ONS 2023 educational slides: PR abbreviation

glossary.caveat: Use this expansion in a response context; PR can have other medical meanings. The required evidence and assessment method depend on the disease and source framework.

glossary.definition: A distinct category used to describe a very good partial treatment response in multiple myeloma.
glossary.sourceLabel: International Myeloma Working Group / International Myeloma Foundation: uniform response criteria

supportingSources.label: International Myeloma Foundation, ONS 2023 educational slides: VGPR abbreviation

glossary.caveat: This entry establishes the myeloma expansion. Other disease frameworks may use VGPR differently; the token does not identify a response-criteria version or imply complete response.

glossary.definition: A response-assessment category describing cancer without a meaningful improvement or worsening under the applicable disease framework.
glossary.sourceLabel: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: stable disease

supportingSources.label: NCI lymphoma trial listing: stable disease (SD) in response assessment

glossary.caveat: Do not expand statistical SD as stable disease; it commonly means standard deviation. Stable disease is not the same as remission, and source-specific assessment rules are not supplied here.

glossary.definition: Cancer that is increasing in extent, spreading, or otherwise worsening.
glossary.sourceLabel: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: progressive disease

supportingSources.label: International Myeloma Workshop Consensus Panel 1 (Blood, 2011): progressive disease (PD)

glossary.caveat: Use only in the disease-response context. This abbreviation does not identify the disease-specific progression rules, assessment date, or evidence used.

glossary.definition: The proportion of assessed patients whose cancer responds to treatment; also termed objective response rate.
glossary.sourceLabel: FDA Oncology Center of Excellence: patient-friendly language for cancer clinical trials
glossary.caveat: ORR is a rate for a defined group, not an individual response category. The source must specify the qualifying response categories, denominator, and assessment framework. No rate is calculated here.

glossary.definition: The time patients remain alive without their disease worsening during or after treatment.
glossary.sourceLabel: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: progression-free survival
glossary.caveat: The time origin, event definition, and censoring rules depend on the study or source. PFS does not mean that the cancer has disappeared. No endpoint is derived here.

glossary.definition: The time patients remain alive from a defined starting point, such as diagnosis or treatment initiation.
glossary.sourceLabel: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: overall survival
glossary.caveat: Preserve the source's time origin and follow-up definition. Overall survival is distinct from a survival percentage at a specified time; neither is derived here.

glossary.definition: An imaging measurement that uses X-rays at two energy levels to assess bone mineral density.
glossary.sourceLabel: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: dual energy X-ray absorptiometry
glossary.context: Bone-density imaging; DEXA and DXA refer to the same technique.
glossary.caveat: A modality label does not establish a measured bone-density value, a diagnosis of osteoporosis, image availability, or myeloma bone lesions. DEXA is not dexamethasone.

glossary.definition: The part of the nervous system comprising the brain and spinal cord.
glossary.sourceLabel: NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms: central nervous system
glossary.context: Anatomy; may qualify oncology involvement, relapse, or prophylaxis fields.
glossary.caveat: CNS alone is an anatomical term. It does not establish CNS disease, CNS prophylaxis, or a CNS-IPI score.

glossary.definition: A clinical prognostic index developed for aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma using features recorded before treatment.
glossary.sourceLabel: International Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma Prognostic Factors Project (N Engl J Med, 1993; PubMed)
glossary.context: Lymphoma prognostic assessment, especially aggressive non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
glossary.caveat: Keep IPI distinct from aaIPI, revised IPI, NCCN-IPI, CNS-IPI, FLIPI, and Hodgkin IPS. This definition neither identifies a field's variant nor assigns a score or risk group.

glossary.definition: An age-adjusted variant of the lymphoma IPI using disease stage, lactate dehydrogenase, and performance status.
glossary.sourceLabel: International Non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma Prognostic Factors Project (N Engl J Med, 1993; PubMed)

supportingSources.label: Leppa et al., Blood Advances 2020: age-adjusted International Prognostic Index (aaIPI)

glossary.caveat: Preserve the source's timing and variant, including any explicitly second-line version. Do not assume aaIPI and IPI are interchangeable or compute a score from this entry.

glossary.definition: A clinical prognostic index developed for follicular lymphoma using features recorded at diagnosis.
glossary.sourceLabel: Solal-Celigny et al., Follicular lymphoma international prognostic index (Blood, 2004; PubMed)
glossary.caveat: Disease-specific: do not use as a generic lymphoma index or equate it with FLIPI2. No score, risk category, or treatment recommendation is supplied.

glossary.definition: A distinct follicular lymphoma prognostic index developed prospectively with progression-free survival as its principal endpoint.
glossary.sourceLabel: Federico et al., Follicular lymphoma international prognostic index 2 (J Clin Oncol, 2009; PubMed)
glossary.caveat: FLIPI2 is distinct from the original FLIPI and should retain its own source label. No component thresholds, score, or risk category are supplied.

glossary.definition: A prognostic score developed for advanced Hodgkin lymphoma using clinical and laboratory features at diagnosis.
glossary.sourceLabel: Hasenclever and Diehl, A prognostic score for advanced Hodgkin's disease (N Engl J Med, 1998; PubMed)

supportingSources.label: NCI SEER: International Prognostic Score (IPS), Hodgkin lymphoma

glossary.context: Advanced Hodgkin lymphoma prognostic assessment only.
glossary.caveat: Use this expansion only when Hodgkin lymphoma prognostic context is explicit. Do not equate IPS with IPI or IPSS, or assume a specific IPS variant from the abbreviation alone. No score or risk group is assigned.
